title: What remains after two half-lives?
hook: Watch an expected radioactive population shrink.

knows: the quantities named in the question
doesNotKnow: Each half-life halves the expected number still present. From 100 to 50, then from 50 to 25.

misconception: The alternative answers in the prediction appear plausible without the stated physical model.
objective: Each half-life halves the expected number still present. From 100 to 50, then from 50 to 25.

claims.text: Each half-life halves the expected number still present. From 100 to 50, then from 50 to 25. The dots represent expected counts, not a prediction of exactly which nuclei decay. Individual decay is random.
claims.source: Radioactive decay expectation N(t)=N0(1/2)^(t/t_half). N0=100 and t=2t_half gives 25.

recall.question: A large radioactive sample has an expected 80 nuclei remaining now. What is its expected count one half-life later?
recall.why: One half-life halves the expected count: 80/2 = 40.
